setting.title: The Wharf Lane Atlas
setting.premise: Ursula Fenn has gathered four old friends in the flat above her canal-side secondhand bookshop for the shop's fortieth birthday weekend. On Friday night, hours after she announced it would go to auction to pay for a new roof, the shop's hand-coloured 1831 canal atlas vanished from its locked cabinet on the shop floor below.
setting.missingItem: a hand-coloured 1831 atlas of the county canals

guests.name: Quentin Achterberg
guests.role: a retired lock-keeper who lives on the narrowboat moored under the shop window
guests.voice: 68. Measured and old-fashioned. Capitals and full stops, sentences a touch long, says 'I dare say' and 'mind you'. Uses ⚓ now and then and no other emoji.

away.status: at the chandlery for a stove part

pressed.text: Asleep by midnight. Nothing wakes me on Patience.

caught.text: All right. I was out on the towpath with my pipe at one o'clock.

She gave Tamsin the key to hang in the kitchen, as she always does.

pressed.text: Ten o'clock, in the cabinet, locked. I watched her turn the key.

lines.text: Nothing worth repeating. The boat is a world of its own at night.

questions.ask: Who do you think took it?

pressed.text: That's all I'll say. He was very taken with it.

questions.ask: What do you make of Saoirse?

pressed.text: Always on her phone after dark. Young people.

pressed.text: She'd give you her last biscuit.

questions.ask: What do you make of Yusuf?

lines.text: Ursula's great-nephew. A good lad under all that phone.

pressed.text: A good lad. Talks to his phone more than to people.

questions.ask: How do you know Ursula?

lines.text: I kept Wharf Lane lock for thirty years. She brought me tea and a paperback every Tuesday. ⚓

questions.ask: Where are you sleeping?

lines.text: On Patience, my boat. Moored right under the shop window.

pressed.text: On the boat. I wouldn't sleep anywhere else.

questions.ask: How was the quiz on Friday?

lines.text: Tamsin read the questions. Saoirse's team won. I carried the canal round, naturally.

questions.ask: Anything odd this morning?

lines.text: The cabinet still locked and the atlas gone.
And the key back on its hook in the kitchen, Saoirse says. Make of that what you will.

pressed.text: Back on its hook. Somebody tidy.

questions.ask: Who had the cabinet key after the viewing?

lines.text: Tamsin. Ursula gave it to her to hang up.
But it was still in her cardigan pocket at twenty to twelve. The brass fish fob was hanging out when she walked me down.

pressed.text: The fish fob. Plain as day, in her pocket.

questions.ask: Did you see anything from the towpath on Friday night?

I thought Ursula must have sent her down. And I could hardly mention it without mentioning the pipe.

pressed.text: It was Tamsin. Nobody else wears that long green cardigan.

questions.ask: What do you make of the auction?

lines.text: It breaks my heart. My lock is on page nine of that atlas.
But a roof is a roof.

pressed.text: A roof is a roof. Ursula knows her own mind.

questions.ask: Tell me about your boat.

lines.text: Patience. Thirty-two foot, older than Yusuf's father, and leaks only when it rains.

questions.ask: Where were you on Saturday night?

lines.text: On the boat by eleven after all that party food.

pressed.text: Eleven. Patience and I keep early hours.

questions.ask: Anything odd this morning?

lines.text: Two cocoa mugs left in the sink. Somebody had a late chat.

questions.ask: What did you do on Saturday?

lines.text: The party. I made a speech about the lock. Too long, Saoirse says.

pressed.text: Twenty minutes is not long for forty years.

questions.ask: Did you hear anything on Saturday night?

lines.text: A young woman on the towpath on her phone after midnight. Saoirse, I should think.

questions.ask: Has anyone tried to save the atlas from the auction?

lines.text: Tamsin has. She's been ringing round the regulars for money for the roof. Quietly.

pressed.text: She has. Every regular in the book.

questions.ask: What did you do on Sunday?

lines.text: Took everyone up to the Lock Inn on Patience. Yusuf steered us into the reeds.

questions.ask: Where were you on Sunday night?

lines.text: In the flat, in Ursula's armchair. The boat stove packed in.

pressed.text: The armchair, all night. My back will tell you.

questions.ask: Anything odd this morning?

lines.text: My hatch was unbolted when I went down at eight. And a small wet footprint on the step.

pressed.text: A small foot. Wet. On my step.

questions.ask: Did you put the atlas's slipcase in your boat locker?

lines.text: I did not. I was in Ursula's armchair all Sunday night. Ask Yusuf, he complained about my snoring.

pressed.text: Not I. I never left the flat.

questions.ask: If you had to name someone today, who would it be?

lines.text: I won't. Not my friends.

questions.ask: When are you heading off?

lines.text: Taking Patience up to the winding hole this afternoon. Then home, which is here.
